subject: MSA & Order Form: proposed assurance tempo, pen-test notice, and evidence handoff
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sasha Cole <sasha.cole@acme-health.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Mar 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: MSA & Order Form: proposed assurance tempo, pen-test notice, and evidence handoff

Hi Sasha —

Thanks for progressing the Order Form / MSA review with your legal team. To help unblock procurement, I wanted to propose a concise assurance “tempo” and a pen-test notice approach we think balances your audit requirements with our operational constraints. High level:

- Evidence cadence: weekly artifact handoff during onboarding (weeks 1–4), then quarterly snapshot deliveries for standard SOC 2 artifacts.
- Pen-test notice: standard 30-day notice for scheduled tests; allow 48-hour emergency notice for critical vulnerability checks with mutually agreed scope.
- Scope: we prefer sampled evidence (assertions + supporting logs/snapshots) rather than unlimited live inspection; we can provide sampled production snapshots, SOC 2 report, and a read-only view into artifact manifests.
- On-call: primary contact during evidence windows will be me; we’ll provide a 24/7 escalation for pen-test windows.

I’ve attached an evidence matrix (evidence_matrix.xlsx) and a pen-test notice template (pen-test-notice-template.pdf) to illustrate format and fields we typically share. Can you confirm: (1) Acme’s preferred inspection window length, and (2) whether your legal team requires an absolute rights clause (we generally limit to scoped, sampled inspections)?

Next steps I propose: we share proposed redlines to the MSA Order Form, agree on sampling bands, and finalize a DocuSign-ready order form. If helpful, I can loop our legal lead (Priyom) for redline language.

Regards,

Jasmine Liu
Solutions Lead, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: evidence_matrix.xlsx] [Attachment: pen-test-notice-template.pdf]

From: Sasha Cole <sasha.cole@acme-health.com>

Cc: Rhea Patel <rhea.patel@acme-health.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Mar 2025 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form: proposed assurance tempo, pen-test notice, and evidence handoff

Thanks Jasmine —

This is a helpful starting point. A couple quick clarifications from Acme Legal/SecOps:

- Inspection window: we prefer a 5 business day window for scheduled evidence inspections, and a max 48-hour window for urgent escalations.
- Live access vs snapshots: legal will push for broader rights by default; SecOps would accept scoped, sampled snapshots if legal is OK with the sampling definition.
- Evidence types: we will need confirmation on whether full raw logs are required or whether indexed, redacted logs + config snapshots are acceptable.

I’ve attached Acme’s vendor questionnaire that highlights specific asks — we’ll fill the operational bits and return. Also looping Rhea (procurement) for the order form timeline.

Sasha Cole
Head of Security Operations
Acme Health
[Attachment: acme_vendor_questionnaire.pdf]

Hi Sasha —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. We’re good with a 5 business day scheduled window and a 48-hour emergency escalation notice as your teams prefer. To keep legal comfortable while keeping inspections operationally feasible, here’s a proposed compromise we can include in the MSA redline:

- Sampling band: evidence requests limited to pre-defined categories (SOC 2 artifacts, config snapshots, redacted indexed logs) and sampled at no more than 3 production-snapshot requests per rolling 12 months without additional commercial terms.
- Notice & scheduling: scheduled inspections require 5 business days notice; pen-test vendor engagements require 30-day advanced notice and a short statement of scope; emergency tests governed by an incident response clause and require mutual sign-off.
- Data handling: all provided artifacts are subject to our redaction rules and must be used solely for audit purposes; no retention beyond 90 days unless mutually agreed.

I’m attaching a draft redline for the Order Form/Appendix that implements the above (redlines_MSA_v3.docx). Priyom — can you please review the proposed language and flag any legal risks or stronger guardrails you’d add?

Thanks —

Jasmine
[Attachment: redlines_MSA_v3.docx]

Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form: proposed assurance tempo, pen-test notice, and evidence handoff

Team —

Reviewed Jasmine’s draft redlines and Acme’s questionnaire. High-level legal notes and a suggested redline approach below (I attached a clean PDF with tracked changes):

1) Audit rights: convert "inspection" language into "evidence production" with scoped categories to avoid unlimited live access. Spell out sampling band (3 snapshots per year) and require a written request specifying artifact categories.

2) Pen-test vendor: require vendor attestation and a signed scope; vendor shall not exfiltrate data, and Redwood will escrow a sanitized snapshot for reproduction if required.

3) Data retention: 90-day retention for artifacts by Acme after delivery; any longer retention requires a commercial review.

4) Timelines: we can commit to evidence delivery SLAs of 5 business days for standard artifacts and 48 hours for critical incident artifacts where feasible; note this will be operationally triaged and may be subject to blackout windows.

5) Exceptions: carveouts for change freeze windows and scheduled maintenance; define a mutual escalation path and a single sign-off owner per inspection.

I’ve recommended language that should be acceptable to most enterprise legal teams while protecting Redwood’s operational surface. Please see attached: proposed_redlines_MSA.pdf and a sample pen-test attestation template (pen-test-notice-template.pdf).

Priyom Das
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_redlines_MSA.pdf] [Attachment: pen-test-notice-template.pdf]

Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form: proposed assurance tempo, pen-test notice, and evidence handoff

Thanks all —

We reviewed Priyom’s language with Acme Legal and SecOps and can accept the sampling band and retention carveouts as written. A few final operational asks before DocuSign:

- Please confirm the process for requesting a production snapshot (form + expected SLA).
- We need a pen-test vendor name field on the order form and confirmation that vendors will sign the attestation (no exfiltration).
- Can Redwood confirm blackout windows and how they’re communicated (we prefer a shared calendar entry and a 30-day notice for major maintenance windows).

I attached our redlined Order Form (Acme_redlines_OrderForm.pdf). Once you confirm the snapshot request process and update the order form to include the vendor attestation checkbox, Rhea will route the DocuSign.

Best,

Sasha Cole
Head of Security Operations
Acme Health
